item.title: Marugame Castle: Towering Stone Walls — Guide
item.description: Marugame Castle is one of Japan’s twelve castles to retain its original wooden keep, and though the keep itself is one of the smallest, the castle is famous for something else: its stone walls. Rising in tiers up the hill of Kameyama, the ramparts are among the tallest and most beautifully curved in Japan, sweeping upward in graceful concave lines to a total height of around 60 metres — a masterpiece of Edo-period stone-fitting.

item.title: Tottori Castle Ruins: Stone Walls Above the City — Guide
item.description: Tottori Castle was a mountain stronghold on Kyusho Hill above the city, remembered above all for the terrible siege of 1581, when the warlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi surrounded and starved the castle into surrender in one of the most brutal blockades of Japan’s warring-states era. The keep is long gone, but extensive stone ramparts survive on the hill and around its base, along with a reconstructed gate and, unusually, the stone-built base of a Meiji-era Western-style building.

item.title: Kofu Castle Ruins (Maizuru Castle Park): The City's Central Historic Park — Guide
item.description: Kofu Castle, also known as Maizuru Castle, was built in the late 16th century, and while the main keep no longer stands, its impressive surviving stone walls, gates and reconstructed turrets remain at the heart of Kofu City as Maizuru Castle Park. The park is a pleasant central green space just a short walk from Kofu Station, with climbable stonework offering views over the city toward the surrounding mountains, making it an easy, free stop for visitors exploring central Kofu on foot.
